summary: VPCE egress: fragmented UDP control payloads rewritten by customer NGFW cause intermittent KV cache heartbeat loss
description: Issue summary: Customer reports intermittent loss of KV-cache heartbeats between serving nodes and the control plane after large control messages are transmitted over their VPCE egress path. Impact: A subset of serving nodes in the customer's private deployment show repeated reconnects to control plane, increased token cost from retries, and transient model shard fetch delays. Hypothesis: Customer NGFW is performing a fragmentation/normalization step (IP ID/fragment offset rewrite) for UDP egress which corrupts reassembly of large UDP datagrams (EDNS0/DNS responses and internal control-plane UDP probes), leading to control-plane heartbeats being dropped and subsequent gRPC backoff cascades. This manifests as intermittent heartbeat timeouts and increased KV-cache miss rates.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Using a serving node in customer VPC, trigger a heavy artifact fetch that produces >1200 byte control-plane UDP responses (simulated via debug tool).
2) Observe pcap on node interface and VPCE ENI concurrently while replicating the fetch.
3) Reproduce with and without NGFW in path (customer provided bypass available during testing window 03/11).
4) Correlate node control-plane logs with pcap and VPCE flow logs to identify dropped fragments and reassembly failures.

investigation_notes: 03/10 11:00 Priya K: Customer attached tcpdump showing fragmented UDP frames where fragment offset sequence is non-monotonic after NGFW egress appliance (pcap attached).

03/10 13:30 Evan L: Verified reassembly failures on node using 'tcpdump -r' and kernel logs. Reproducible when EDNS0 responses >1280 bytes are mirrored through customer's NGFW. When NGFW bypassed, fragments reassemble cleanly and heartbeats remain stable.
03/10 15:10 SRE: VPCE ENI flow logs show symmetric flow but several fragments are marked with different IP ID and inconsistent MF flags (indicates rewrite/normalization).

03/11 09:40 Network Eng (customer): Confirmed NGFW has 'fragmentation normalization' policy which rewrites IP ID/offset on egress to preserve session affinity for stateful inspection. They are able to disable this policy for test subnets.
03/11 10:05 Support: After disabling normalization for test subnet, observed zero heartbeat timeouts over 30m load test. KV-cache miss rate returned to baseline.
comments: 2026-03-10 11:12 Priya Kapoor: Customer (Nimbus) opened ticket — intermittent serving nodes dropping control plane heartbeats. They provided pcap + kernel logs. Marked as P1 due to production impact.

2026-03-10 12:40 Evan Liu: Started triage. Early kernel evidence shows fragment reassembly failures. Suspect network device rewriting fragment headers. Requesting customer to run tcpdump at VPCE ENI and behind NGFW for comparison.

2026-03-10 16:05 Nimbus-Network (Anika S): Collected pcaps and flow logs, attached to ticket. NGFW vendor (NetFiltr) has fragmentation normalization enabled by default for UDP. We can test disabling on a small subnet Friday 03/11 09:00-11:00 UTC.

2026-03-11 11:45 Evan Liu: Confirmed disabling normalization removes the failure mode. Still collecting post-test metrics. Recommending configuration change or adding MTU/DF adjustments to avoid large UDP control payloads.

2026-03-12 09:03 Priya Kapoor: Customer applied permanent change to NGFW (disable IP fragment normalization for Redwood control-plane destinations). Monitoring over 24h showed no recurrence. Preparing resolution notes and follow-up guidance.
2026-03-12 15:26 SRE (Jordan Blake): Filed internal playbook update to add 'check NGFW fragment normalization' to VPCE network checklist. Linked in related_confluence_pages.
resolution: Workaround applied: customer disabled 'fragmentation normalization' policy on their NGFW for traffic destined to Redwood control-plane and VPCE endpoints. Post-change verification: no heartbeat timeouts observed during 24h monitoring window, KV-cache miss rates normalized. Recommended next steps: 1) Customer to keep policy disabled for Redwood subnets or create exception rules that exclude control-plane UDP/EDNS traffic. 2) Engineering follow-up: add detection to serving runtime to surface UDP reassembly failures earlier and log clearer indicators. 3) Docs: update VPCE onboarding checklist with NGFW fragment normalization guidance.
